item.title: Students at Cornell Daily Sun Pursued Sexual Assault Case for Two Years
item.description: The student newspaper, The Cornell Daily Sun, covered the allegations of rape at a fraternity house since they were first made in 2024 and led the reporting on the case.
item.dc:creator: Emma Goldberg
item.media:credit: Heather Ainsworth for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Cornell Daily Sun is independent of the university and has its offices off campus.

item.title: A Timeline of the Cornell University Rape Investigation
item.description: Prosecutors have reopened an investigation into a former student’s claims that several men sexually assaulted her in a campus fraternity house.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Barnes
item.media:credit: Heather Ainsworth for The New York Times
item.media:description: Cornell University administrators and the Tompkins County district attorney are under pressure over their handling of a former student’s allegations.

item.title: Dartmouth Provost Is the Latest College Professor Examined for A.I. Use
item.description: Dartmouth said it would investigate its provost over A.I. accusations. Similar controversies on other campuses have prompted frustration among students.
item.dc:creator: Mark Arsenault and Alan Blinder
item.media:credit: Caleb Kenna for The New York Times
item.media:description: Dartmouth College’s president has encouraged A.I., but now the school is investigating how one of its professors used A.I.

item.title: MacArthur Foundation Announces 2026 ‘Genius Grant’ Winners
item.description: The 20 fellowship recipients across the arts, humanities and sciences will each receive an $800,000, no-strings-attached stipend for their work.

item.title: Cornell’s Chi Phi Chapter Faces Scrutiny Over Assault Accusations
item.description: Chi Phi’s Cornell chapter was shuttered after a woman said its members sexually assaulted her. It was one of the oldest fraternities at the school, where Greek life has thrived.
item.dc:creator: Alan Blinder and Michael S. Schmidt
item.media:credit: Heather Ainsworth for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Chi Phi fraternity house at Cornell University.

item.title: University of Michigan Halts New Grading Plan After Backlash From Critics
item.description: The program was intended to address what the university called a “mental health crisis.” But the plan was met with criticism that it was coddling students.
item.dc:creator: Madaleine Rubin
item.media:credit: Sylvia Jarrus for The New York Times
item.media:description: The University of Michigan campus in Ann Arbor.

item.title: As Mr. Belding on “Saved by the Bell,” Dennis Haskins Made Principals Your Pal

item.title: College Students Flex Their Power in A.I. Investment Frenzy
item.description: Dorm Room Fund, a program that lets college students invest in their peers, raised a new $50 million fund as the competition for young founders ramps up.

item.media:description: Molly Fowler, a partner at Dorm Room Fund, at her office in Manhattan. The venture capital firm has raised a new $50 million fund.

item.title: U.S. News Shuffled Its N.Y. High School Rankings. An Uproar Ensued.
item.description: After the New York State Education Department denied a request from U.S. News for A.P. scores, perennially top-ranked schools plummeted.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Haag
item.media:credit: Mimi d’Autremont for The New York Times
item.media:description: Robert Kravitz, superintendent of Jericho Union Free School District on Long Island, was upset when his school’s rating plummeted.

item.title: Donor Gives $3 Billion to Carnegie Mellon, the Largest University Gift Ever
item.description: The donation by Kenneth Griffin, intended mostly to help build a campus in Miami, was the biggest single gift in the history of U.S. higher education.
item.dc:creator: Alan Blinder
item.media:credit: Martina Tuaty for The New York Times
item.media:description: The donation from the hedge fund executive Kenneth C. Griffin is more than the record $2 billion gift given to Oregon Health and Science University recently.

item.title: Cornell Sexual Assault Investigation to Be Reopened
item.description: After outrage over allegations in a lawsuit, the Tompkins County district attorney will revisit the decision not to pursue criminal charges against seven fraternity members.
item.dc:creator: Sharon Otterman and Hurubie Meko
item.media:credit: Seth Wenig/Associated Press
item.media:description: District Attorney Matthew Van Houten said his office would reopen the investigation into an alleged 2024 sexual assault following community outrage.

item.title: 30 Ideas for Fixing U.S. Schools, Ranked by Experts
item.description: Math and reading scores are in a decade-long slump. We asked three dozen experts: What could turn things around?

item.title: Why China Is Requiring Ninth Graders to Read ‘Jane Eyre’
item.description: The Victorian heroine has long been celebrated in China for her independence and insistence on equality.
item.dc:creator: Yan Zhuang and Li You
item.media:credit: Zhu Zhenqiang/VCG, via Getty Images
item.media:description: A woman reads at a bookstore in Beijing in August. “Jane Eyre” has found generations of readers in China since it was first translated into Chinese a century ago.

item.title: At U.C.L.A., a Bollywood Dance Team Like ‘Best of the Best’
item.description: “For a lot of South Asians, dance is the way we connect,” said a member of the U.C.L.A. team Nashaa. Our photographer captured glimpses of the team last year, from audition to competitions.
item.dc:creator: Gabriela Bhaskar and Brian Seibert

item.title: Statement Written by Police in Cornell Assault Case Omitted Her Claim She Was Raped
item.description: Documents obtained by The New York Times show that the campus police at Cornell University sent a condensed statement to a prosecutor, who then declined to bring charges.
item.dc:creator: Hurubie Meko
item.media:credit: Heather Ainsworth for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Cornell Police Department summarized hours of interviews with a woman who said she was raped into a six-page document that excluded key details. A local prosecutor did not pursue criminal charges based on that document.

item.title: The Cornell Rape Investigation: Five Takeaways
item.description: The New York Times obtained more than 1,000 pages from the university’s internal inquiry into accusations by “Jane Doe.” Here are the revelations so far.
item.dc:creator: Sharon Otterman
item.media:credit: Heather Ainsworth for The New York Times
item.media:description: Cornell University’s investigation of a 2024 sexual assault allegation included interviews, emails and screenshots.

item.title: How a Cornell Student Went From Shame to Anger
item.description: The woman known as “Jane Doe” was initially embarrassed about what happened at a fraternity party in 2024, but soon concluded: “I was assaulted.”
item.dc:creator: Debra Kamin, Matt Flegenheimer and Amy Julia Harris
item.media:credit: Heather Ainsworth for The New York Times
item.media:description: Prosecutors have reopened the case of a woman who said she was sexually assaulted by Cornell University fraternity brothers in 2024.

item.title: Cornell’s Jane Doe Said She Was Given Ketamine. Here’s How the Drug Works.
item.description: Ketamine is a short-acting anesthetic that can have hallucinogenic effects. It is becoming more easily available, and some experts fear misuse is increasing.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Jacobs
item.media:credit: Julie Ezvan/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images
item.media:description: Ketamine can have a hallucinogenic effect at certain doses.

item.title: Cornell Will Hire Outside Lawyers to Investigate 2024 Rape Claim
item.description: The university and law enforcement officials are under growing pressure to explain how they handled a woman’s initial claims of being assaulted by a group of students.
item.dc:creator: Christopher Maag
item.media:credit: Victor J. Blue for The New York Times
item.media:description: Gov. Kathy Hochul said that parents should be able to feel confident that their children are safe when attending college.

item.title: What New York’s Rape Laws Mean for the Cornell Case
item.description: State law makes it harder to prosecute when victims drank willingly. The prosecutor in the Cornell case said that kept him from charging students accused of sexual assault.
item.dc:creator: Maria Cramer
item.media:credit: Mary Altaffer/Associated Press

item.title: Cornell Students Question Greek Life Culture After Sexual Assault Claim

item.media:description: Media outlets have descended on the Cornell campus in recent days after the district attorney announced he is reopening the investigation into a 2024 sexual assault case.

item.title: Students at Cornell Divided Over Sexual Assault Investigation
item.description: In this episode of “The Call,” host Natalie Kitroeff calls the reporter Emma Goldberg, who’s on Cornell’s campus interviewing students as they grapple with the explosive news that prosecutors are reopening a 2024 sexual assault investigation into seven members of Cornell’s Chi Phi fraternity.
